rationale: Evidence from iteration 2 (score 442.8): the oval finishes 15/20 (progress 0.95, 1.93 s), the s-bend finishes 3/20 (progress 0.75), and the slalom never finishes (progress 0.33, max_error about 0.063 m, just above the fixed 0.06 m off-track limit). Iteration 1 to 2 showed that slower speed and a finer sensor spread helped the bends, but the robot still leaves the line on sharp alternating bends. The body-width term cannot raise the off-track limit (it is 0.06 m for every allowed body width), so tracking error has to fall. Hypothesis H4: at base_speed 1.2 the robot covers ground faster than its steering can follow, and the sensor span of +/-0.045 m is still too narrow, so the line leaves the sensor footprint during large swings. Changes: (1) base_speed 1.2 to 1.0. The oval time limit has headroom (about 2.3 s expected against 3 s), and completion is worth 500 points while time is worth at most 60. (2) Sensor span widened to +/-0.06 m (seven sensors, 0.02 m spacing, y = 0.04 m), so the line stays visible at larger lateral error. (3) Weights scaled to keep their ends at +/-2 and their spacing even: [-2, -1.33, -0.67, 0, 0.67, 1.33, 2]. The signal gain per metre falls from about 44 to about 33, so kp rises from 2.0 to 2.6 to keep the overall steering gain similar (about 86 vs 88 per metre). (4) kd kept at 0.6 for damping, and ki at 0.05. Mass 0.6 kg, track 0.12 m, and radius 0.03 m are unchanged to isolate the speed and sensing effects. Expected result: slalom progress well above 0.33, with some completions on the s-bend, and max_error nearer 0.05 m. Risks: kp 2.6 with kd 0.6 may add jitter (steering_oscillation was 0.38 on the oval), and the wider span could reduce resolution on gentle bends. Measurements wanted next: completion and progress per track to see whether slower speed or the wider span drove the change; max_error and line_loss_events on the slalom to test H4; steering_oscillation to check whether kp 2.6 adds jitter; and completion_time on the oval to confirm the time budget.
